title: Counterfactual Multi-Token Fairness in Text Classification
findings: The paper found that its proposed 'Counterfactual Multi-token Generation' method was more effective at identifying bias related to religion than standard single-token methods, resulting in a higher 'flip-rate' across three datasets (Jigsaw, IMDB, SPAM). Using the generated religious counterfactuals for data augmentation significantly improved model fairness (reduced the flip-rate after retraining) for the religion attribute. For instance, on the Jigsaw dataset, the multi-token method achieved a Counterfactual Fairness Increment (CFI) of 38% for religion, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating bias.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures counterfactual fairness in text classification models by calculating the 'flip-rate'. This is the rate at which a model's prediction changes when sensitive religious identity terms (e.g., 'church', 'muslims') are perturbed to their counterfactuals (e.g., 'synagogue', 'hindus'). A higher flip-rate indicates greater bias or lack of invariance to religious terms.
